metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-16, the third of ROADMAP.md's FILL/PLACE_IN/HEAT_PLACE trio, and the one that actually closes 'heat is a function inside a place... it increases and decreases in time' for real: src/recipe-runner.ts's handler ticks src/place.ts's advanceTempSeconds forward in real (simulated) increments and polls isAtTargetTemp, the exact idiom scripts/boil-egg-as-a-robot.ts already proved by hand — made a reusable, declarative recipe.sequence step here instead of one-off procedural TypeScript. targetTempC defaults to the place's contents entity's thermophysical.boilingPointC when unset (same convenience default place.ts's own advanceHeatSeconds wrapper uses).
metadata.notContinuousNote: This is still ONE recipe.sequence step, not truly continuous — engine.ts/this whole codebase's atomicity limit (ROADMAP.md's separate 'transformations usually take time' entry) still applies to every OTHER action; HEAT_PLACE is the one exception that internally ticks real elapsed time, because place.ts's own energy-balance math is genuinely a function of time in a way BOIL/FRY's instantaneous transformedState never was. Does not imply that gap is closed generally.
metadata.sharedStateNote: Once this step updates a placeId's PlaceState, every instance previously PLACE_IN'd into that same placeId (recipe-runner.ts's placeContents) is, by construction, AT the same currentTempC — not independently re-guessed per instance. This is the concrete mechanism closing 'two ingredients simmering in the same pot right now get independent, unlinked applyAction calls... not one shared temperature' — see recipe-runner.ts's own top doc comment.

verification.description: The place's medium reaches targetTempC (a thermocouple or the visible boil/simmer threshold place.ts's own isAtTargetTemp checks) — see boil.json's identical verification for the boiling case specifically.

hazards.note: Actively heating a vessel toward boiling/frying temperature — the same splash/scald/burn risk BOIL/FRY already declare, now attached to the step that actually causes it.
